steps.intent: Initialize the authenticated Archer command without navigating to an unvalidated destination.

steps.userPrompt: Write every user-facing status or explanation you print in English. Never invent footage content, dialogue, or events that are not present in the supplied source file -- you are editing real, user-approved footage only, not generating new video. Step 1: clone https://github.com/browser-use/video-use.git into your working directory (do not assume it is already present) and follow its own install.md exactly to set it up -- install ffmpeg/ffprobe if missing, install its Python dependencies (requests, librosa, matplotlib, pillow, numpy) via `uv sync` or `pip install -e .`, and confirm ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is present in the environment before proceeding (it is provided to you as an environment variable; if it is missing, stop and report that clearly instead of guessing or fabricating a key). Step 2: download the real source footage from {{context.intakeContext.footage_url}} into the project directory -- if this value is blank, stop immediately and report that no footage URL was supplied rather than guessing one. Step 3: read video-use's own SKILL.md and reference docs end to end before editing anything, and follow its documented workflow exactly (it manages its own project.md state file -- create and use one). Step 4: your top priority is burned-in titles and word-level, speech-synced captions: run video-use's transcription step (ElevenLabs Scribe, word-level timestamps) and use its native captioning approach to burn in synced subtitle text, defaulting to two-word uppercase chunks synced to speech unless the user's own instructions in this prompt say otherwise; add a clear title card/overlay for the event or moment being shown, grounded only in what the footage and any provided event details actually show. Apply video-use's other default enhancements (filler-word/dead-space removal, color grade, audio fades at cuts) only if they do not risk cutting content the user needs -- prioritize caption accuracy and timing above cosmetic edits, and if any step fails, continue with the remaining pipeline rather than aborting the whole edit. Step 5: run video-use's own self-evaluation step on the final render before finishing. Step 6: write the final rendered file to /home/user/output/final.mp4 exactly (create the directory if needed) -- this exact path is what the platform will read back after you finish; do not use any other path or filename. Step 7: in your final message, state the output path you wrote, a one-paragraph summary of what was captioned/titled, and any step of video-use's pipeline that failed or was skipped and why.

commitMessage: Add Archer video captions/titles workflow using video-use
